blogTitle: FADING EMBER // tour diary (we have not toured) // lineup history
about: thanks for the add!! we're FADING EMBER, a screamo band from Mansfield, Ohio. we sound like the inside of a hoodie at 3 am, but with a bridge. our demo 'Cold Hands, Warm Amps' is 4 songs, $3 at shows or free if you tell 3 friends. current lineup: vocals, guitar, bass, and a drum machine named Dr. Beat who has never missed a practice. former members: 14 (see about me, part 2). we are always looking for a drummer, a second guitarist, and a van. we will play anywhere with an outlet. we scream about the abyss and we are SO happy you're here. (we're fine.)
aboutMore: a note on the lineup. we keep an alumni list and mail every former member a card on their birthday. they're still FADING EMBER in spirit. the Alumni Association meets the first Sunday of the month at the Dairy Dip. attendance: 11 of 14. Big Tom came to every one even after he left to join a ska band, which we're fine with. (this is the vocalist. hi. i'm Cory. i type 'we' because the band is bigger than me. it's not. but it's bigger than me.)
meet: Who we'd like to meet: a drummer who stays. a van owner with an open heart and a sliding door. the sound man at the VFW hall (we have a note for him, written on the back of a flyer). Saosin, just to say we're a band too. anybody who has asked 'are you guys the ones from the garage' and then actually listened to track 3. and whoever invented the word 'bridge,' because we owe you a tribute.

interests.General: the demo (4 songs, $3), flyers (MS Paint, 11 versions of each), load-in, the 10 seconds of soundcheck we get, the storage unit (52 degrees, 1 outlet, a neighbor with a very large ceramic angel collection), Dr. Beat (technically a metronome with pads, we've made peace), alumni birthday cards, merch (a CD-R and a sticker), the first Sunday of the month
interests.Music: Saosin, Thursday, Funeral for a Friend, Finch, Silverstein, Alexisonfire, Underoath, From Autumn to Ashes, Taking Back Sunday (the early records), Dashboard Confessional (the loud-quiet-loud ones), Static Prophecy (Greg put us on a bill, we owe him an amp cable)
interests.Movies: Donnie Darko (everyone says that, so do we), The Crow, Edward Scissorhands, Napoleon Dynamite (rest day), The Lion King (the vocalist cries at the stampede and it's in a song)
interests.Television: Fuse at 4 PM (the screamo block), Invader Zim (sorry, Misery), the weather channel (the only thing that goes down on purpose), reruns of MythBusters
interests.Books: the lyrics notebook (labeled MATH so nobody reads it), the tour budget spreadsheet (it's mostly gas money), The Giving Tree (the vocalist cried at 12 and has not recovered), the oil change price list (the vocalist's day job)
interests.Heroes: the sound man at the VFW hall, every drummer who ever sat behind the kit, Big Tom (the best one), Greg's dad (the extension cord), the lemonade lady next door to the garage, Dee at Perk Avenue (she clapped), Penny (the pick, the bracelet), whoever cleans up after load-out

thanksAdd: thanks for the add!!! we're FADING EMBER. check out our demo 'Cold Hands, Warm Amps' (4 songs, $3, free if you tell 3 friends). we'd like to formally welcome you to the Fading Ember family (it's us, Dr. Beat, 14 alumni, and now you). our next show is TBD. our lineup is TBD. our hearts are 100% not TBD. we're so happy you're here. ambient: current lineup (as of 4:15 pm): vocals, guitar, bass, Dr. Beat. as of 4:16: vocals, guitar, Dr. Beat. a bassist said 'it's not you, it's community college.' we love community college.

storage unit update: the neighbor in unit 15 has a collection of ceramic angels. she came to practice today. she said 'is this the loud kind or the sad kind.' we said 'yes.' she gave us a thumbs up and a cookie.

we wrote a song in the oil change bay today (the vocalist did). it's called 'Cabin Air Filter (Part 1).' it's about replacing something that was fine for 12,000 miles. we think it will hit people hard.
did you know 14 people have been in this band? we'd like to thank all of them. in a card. there will be cake. the first Sunday. the Dairy Dip. be there.
if you're at a show and the drummer looks like he's seen something, that's not drama. that's a drummer. we love them. we're looking for one.
saltyDm: we saw that you denied our request. that's okay. we're a screamo band, we've been denied by experts. flyers on your wall by Friday (virtually). our demo is still $3. our offer is still free if you tell 3 friends. please tell 3 friends. any 3. we'll take what we can get.

keywords.demo: 'Cold Hands, Warm Amps.' 4 songs: 'Apology to the Sun,' 'Parking Lot Funeral,' 'Carbon Copy Heart,' and 'Dr. Beat Is a Machine (We Love Him).' $3 at shows, free if you tell 3 friends. recorded in a basement on a laptop with a mic that is mostly a sock.
keywords.drummer: we're currently seeing other drummers. the current one is Dr. Beat (a metronome with pads, never late, never quits, never smiles). past ones: 14. we're not bitter. we send them cards. one's in a ska band. he's happy. we're so happy for him.
keywords.lineup: we've had 14 lineups since March. Static Prophecy has had 1. we think about that. we don't know what it means. we just think about it. current lineup: ask us tomorrow.
keywords.screamo: it's like emo but we mean it harder and we apologize less. our sound is described by our mothers as 'a lot.' by our fans as 'a lot, in a good way.' by us as 'the inside of a hoodie at 3 am, with a bridge.'
keywords.show: next show is TBD. last show: the Friday garage bill, 9 minutes (the extension cord rule), one lemonade lady, and a standing ovation of one (Chad). we're booking. find us. we're in a storage unit behind the car wash. it's a little cold.

greg: greg we'd like to apologize for the drum machine volume. Dr. Beat has one setting and it's 'emotional.' your dad's kitchen timer went off at 9 minutes and we stopped. he nodded. we nodded. most professional moment of our career.
greg 14 lineups since March. you've had 1. we're not saying you're boring. we're saying we're jealous. teach us stability. we'll pay in demos.
misery: misery thank you for the 11 comments on our flyer. you were the only one who noticed the typo (it said screamoo). we kept it. it's the logo now.

misery we heard you want us to play your birthday. we'd love to. we'll need an outlet, 10 feet of clearance, and a promise that nobody films the part where the vocalist climbs the amp. (it's a hobby.)
lucas: lucas we used your line about the dishwasher. we didn't change it. we put your name on the flyer. it says 'lyrics: lucas (one line).' we hope that's okay. we know it's one line. it's the best line.
lucas you asked to scream a single word. we say yes. the word is 'dishwasher.' we'll cue you at 2:14 of track 3. you have until then to feel something.
vince: vince thank you for TEEN NITE. we'd do it again. we'd bring a drummer. we'll bring 2 drummers. one will be a machine. we'll be fine.
vince 'first 50 people free' is a beautiful phrase. we want it printed on the demo cover. we only need 3 people to come to make it true.
evan: evan we got your note. we put it in the folder with the other 3. we read the line where you said our set was 'sincere.' we won't read into it. we read into it. we think you're a good person. we'd like to do a split.

evan you carried our amp up greg's driveway. we didn't ask. you didn't say. that was the whole thing. we wrote you a thank-you note back. it says thank you. it's the whole note. we learned it from you.
skip: skip we're not looking at the picture of big tom smiling. we're looking at the picture of big tom smiling. he's so happy. we're so happy for him. we're writing a bridge about it. it's called 'Major Key.' it's a joke. it's also a song.
skip we'd like to say yes to the split. 20 minutes each. you bring the horns, we bring Dr. Beat. we'll call it 'The Offbeat Abyss.' you're welcome to the name. we thought of it at 3 am.
darkangel: darkangel we accept 'crimson tears (part 7)' as a song title. we'd like parts 1 through 6 as well. we'll make a concept album. we'll need a drummer. we'll need a cello. we'll need to cry a little.
darkangel your poems on our wall are better than our lyrics. we'd like to hire you. we pay in demos and sandwiches.

dms: {you} we have a question. if a band has 14 lineups in 6 months, is it a band or a rotating exhibit? asking for the vocalist. he's fine.

storage unit update: the ceramic angel lady in unit 15 brought us a casserole. she said 'you boys are too thin to be that loud.' we said thank you. the casserole was great. the vocalist has been in a good mood for 2 days.

we want to tell you about the rink show. we played TEEN NITE right after Cotton Eyed Joe. nobody told the DJ. he said 'and now, a band.' a kid skated backwards in time to the breakdown. best moment of our career. no cameras.

the vocalist's day job is at the oil change place on Route 30. he says 'would you like a cabin air filter' 40 times a day. it's the same voice, just quieter. he says it's good practice for the bridge.

we mailed Big Tom a birthday card. it said 'happy birthday, we're so happy for you.' he wrote back 'thanks, i'm so happy for you too.' we think he means it. we cried in the unit. the angel lady came over with a tissue.
question: how do you tell a guitarist the quiet part is the loud part? asking for the vocalist, who is also the guitarist right now.
do you have a van. it doesn't have to be good. it has to have wheels and a side door. we have a lot of amps and a very small hope.

we got a bracelet from Penny that says IT GETS BETTER. we wear it on the mic hand. we wore it to the garage show and it got better. we're not sure it was the bracelet. we're keeping the bracelet. we sent her a guitar pick with a tiny heart on it.

blog.title: TEEN NITE, FADING EMBER, AND A BOY ON SKATES (a review)
blog.body: we were booked for the 9:30 slot at the Rollerdome. at 9:28 the DJ said 'and now, a band' and played Cotton Eyed Joe by mistake. we stood there. 40 kids skating in circles. the song ended. we started. the first scream hit the disco ball and the ball did something. a boy about 11 skated backwards the entire song and kept eye contact with the vocalist. at the breakdown he did a spin. 7 people showed up for us: 3 stood by the wall, 4 skated, and 1 was a rink employee who asked if we could do it 'a little less.' we did it a little less. Vince said we were gonna be HUGE. we think he meant volume. we got paid in pizza. after, the boy skated up and said 'was that sad?' we said yes. he said 'cool.' that was the whole review. we're so grateful. we're printing it.

blog.title: THE ALUMNI ASSOCIATION (a history of everyone who ever left)
blog.body: 1) Brandon (drums, March): left because of 'a thing.' we still don't know what. sends a postcard every August. 2) Tanner (bass, April): left for community college. sends calculus jokes. 3) Big Tom (drums, May to July): left for a ska band. sends cake. 4) Colby (guitar, 11 days): found a new hobby. it was woodworking. he made us a pick holder. 5) Zach (bass, one weekend): just wanted to see what it was like. 6 and 7) the two Dylans (both drums, different weeks, never met). 8 to 14) we'll do them next time. we meet the first Sunday of the month at the Dairy Dip. nobody orders. we share a sundae. there are 14 spoons. the vocalist always says 'thanks for coming, you were all great.' they always say 'we know.' then everybody laughs. that's the meeting. that's the whole meeting. it's the best thing we do.

blog.title: we wrote a song at the oil change place (a process)
blog.body: the vocalist's day job is at the oil change place on Route 30. it's a pit. you stand under the car and look up. it's a very good place to write a song because every customer is a stranger and every stranger has a story that's mostly about a funny noise. today a lady said 'it makes a sound like it's trying to say something.' he wrote that on a rag. 'Cabin Air Filter (Part 1)' is about the thing in your car nobody looks at until it's 12,000 miles overdue. it's a metaphor. he's not going to say for what. it has 2 screams and a bridge and a quiet part where the vocalist just says 'it was fine' over and over. the manager heard it and said 'is that about the filter?' he said yes. the manager said 'that's the best thing anybody's ever said about a filter.' that's our whole career. that's the bridge.
